description:
Tracking epic that validates `tui2` matches `tui`'s behavior across every user-facing feature. When this epic closes, `tui2` is the recommended default and `tui` is a candidate for sunset.

Per `docs/tui-architecture.md`. Not a single ticket; a tracking epic with one child per feature/area to validate.

## Known today

**The validation surface.**
Every user-visible behavior of `tui` must work identically (or measurably better) in `tui2`. Categories:

- **Rendering correctness** — frames look right, colors match, wrapping works on narrow terminals, OSC 133 zones land.
- **Input handling** — every keybinding works, kill ring, undo, autocomplete, history, paste, multi-line input.
- **Streaming** — agent responses stream smoothly, tick coalescing keeps the UI responsive, no flicker on long responses.
- **Modals/overlays** — model selector, session selector, settings, login dialog, tree selector, summarize prompt, user message selector — all work, focus is correct, Esc cancels, Enter confirms.
- **Custom widgets** — extension UI (`Coder.Extensions.UI`) renders correctly.
- **Resize** — terminal resize is handled cleanly without artifacts.
- **Theme** — all themes render correctly.
- **Edge cases** — empty input, very long input, very long messages, many tool calls, deep tree navigation, long autocomplete lists.
- **Performance** — keystroke latency, frame time on long transcripts, memory usage.

**Per-feature children.**
Each child ticket: "Validate <feature> in tui2." Acceptance: feature works the same as in `tui`, manual test passes, screenshot/recording attached if visual.

**Performance benchmarks.**
At least one performance child: "tui2 keystroke latency on a 500-message transcript ≤ tui's." Concrete numeric targets, not vibes.

**Crash regression.**
Any panic / crash that's been fixed in `tui` (e.g. recent dialyzer fixes, the tree_selector navigation fix from recent commits) is verified to either not exist in `tui2` (different code path) or has been ported.

## Open questions

1. **Per-feature children granularity.** One child per slot? Per modal? Per keybinding category? My lean: per slot for rendering, per keybinding category for input, per modal for overlays. ~25-40 children total.

2. **Automated test parity vs. manual validation.** Some behaviors are unit-testable (key handler reducers); others need manual driver runs. Decide what gets a test, what gets a screenshot/recording, what gets a checklist.

3. **When does `tui2` become the default?** Defaulting to `tui2` is a separate, observable change from "tui2 reaches parity." Two stages: (a) parity reached, opt-in remains the default; (b) flip default to `tui2`, `tui` becomes opt-in. Stage (b) probably gets its own ticket and its own announcement.

4. **What counts as "feature parity"?** `tui2` is allowed to be *better* than `tui`, but it shouldn't regress. Need a published list of what's intentionally changed vs. what must match.

5. **How do we handle bugs found in `tui` during this work?** If we find a bug in `tui` while validating `tui2`, do we fix it in `tui` (it's frozen) or only in `tui2`? Lean: fix in `tui2` only; document in `tui`'s known-issues. `tui` stays frozen.

## Dependencies

Runs continuously alongside `opi-screen` — every default component implementation in `opi-screen` produces a parity child here.

## Out of scope

- The deletion of `octo_pi_tui` (a separate, later epic, intentionally unscheduled).
- Net-new features in `tui2` beyond parity (those are post-cutover work).
title: [EPIC] octo_pi_tui2 behavioral parity with octo_pi_tui
